📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, archiviata la sosta per le nazionali, il Milan si prepara a tornare in campo con l'obiettivo di dare continuità ai risultati e alle buone prestazioni mostrate prima della pausa. Stasera alle 18:00, a San Siro, i rossoneri ospiteranno il Frosinone di Alvini, una delle squadre rivelazione di questa prima parte di stagione.

Alphadjo Cissé è senza dubbio uno degli uomini più in forma. L'ex Catanzaro, con otto reti realizzate dall'inizio della stagione, è il miglior marcatore della squadra. Nelle ultime due gare di Serie A giocate da titolare ha trovato il gol tre volte, con una rete contro il Genoa e una doppietta contro il Bologna. Contro il Frosinone sembrava destinato alla panchina, ma il viaggio transoceanico di Pulisic potrebbe offrirgli una nuova chance dal primo minuto.

In a recent development, prima di procedere con il secondo pronostico sul match, dai un'occhiata alle quote +EV elaborate dalla nostra Intelligenza Artificiale. Il software, stimando la probabilità reale di ogni evento, segnala automaticamente quando un bookmaker sottovaluta un esito, evidenziando le opportunità a Valore Atteso Positivo.

Nella tabella TOP +EV BETS che vedi di seguito troverai le migliori proposte in tempo reale sulla gara. Ma come si leggono queste statistiche? Ora te lo spiego:.

* Giocata consigliata: sulla sinistra trovi subito il mercato consigliato, con subito sotto anche tutti i dati sul tipo di competizione e le info su partita, data e orario; * Migliore Quota: sulla destra trovi la miglior quota presente sul mercato in quel momento sulla giocata consigliata; * EV: subito sotto la quota trovi anche il Valore Atteso Positivo sul mercato, in percentuale.

It has been revealed that tre gol stagionali, uno dei quali su calcio di rigore per Gonçalo Ramos che è inevitabilmente uno dei giocatori più discussi della Serie A. Pesano i 73 milioni spesi fin qui dal Milan che stanno probabilmente incidendo anche sul rendimento. Per Amorim resta un giocatore insostituibile e col Portogallo ha fatto vedere che è anche un abile realizzatore, se messo nelle condizioni di farlo. Domenica a San Siro avrà una nuova occasione per svoltare la propria stagione.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 11:27 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:55 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Manchester United have laid on a private jet for Mauricio Pochettino to fly straight to England in the early hours of Wednesday morning after he finishes work as US national team coach.
  • Pochettino’s last game in charge is against Haiti in Cincinnati, which kicks off at midnight on Tuesday UK time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 11:27 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:55 EST, 16 November 2026.

Manchester United have laid on a private jet for Mauricio Pochettino to fly straight to England in the early hours of Wednesday morning after he finishes work as US national team coach.

Pochettino’s last game in charge is against Haiti in Cincinnati, which kicks off at midnight on Tuesday UK time. The 54-year-old will speak to the media and say farewell to his players before jumping on a plane to Manchester which has been organised by United.

It will enable Pochettino to sleep before he lands in the UK on Wednesday morning ready to go straight to Carrington and start work.

He will be accompanied by first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott.

It has emerged that three other members of his trusted coaching team – assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino – were allowed to travel to Manchester at the weekend after the US won the first leg against Haiti 6-0 in Miami.

According to recent reports, it means that Pochettino’s back-room staff have been able to make a headstart in their preparations for his first game in charge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. It is a huge fixture in the calendar for United, but even more so because he takes over a team languishing in the relegation zone.

Man United have laid on a private jet for Mauricio Pochettino to fly straight to England after he finishes work as US national team coach.

Pochettino will take charge of his final match as USA boss in Cincinnati before boarding the direct flight to Manchester.

Pochettino's long-time assistant Jesus Perez is one of three trusted staff members who have already been given permission to travel to Manchester.

Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty, and is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference on Friday lunchtime.

Speaking ahead of the second leg against Haiti at the TQL Stadium, Pochettino stated: ‘I am with Miguel, Sylvia and Alec and after they are going to join me in Manchester.

‘The next question is where are Jesus, Toni and Sebastiano? They are ahead. After the game (in Miami), they flew to Manchester and they are there in advance. That was the initiative when we agreed terms with Manchester United and with the US national team.

‘They are there preparing everything because on Wednesday, when we arrive, it’s going to be non-stop and then we start with playing games.’.

Il presidente vuole essere vicino a staff e calciatori; il rapporto con l'allenatore si rafforza sulla fiducia reciproca.

Gennaro Gattuso e Claudio Lotito hanno cenato insieme a Formello, in un clima di crescente intesa tra l'allenatore e il presidente della Lazio. Secondo quanto riportato dall'edizione odierna del Corriere della Sera, l'incontro si è tenuto ieri ed è stato un'occasione per parlare della squadra e delle dinamiche interne al centro sportivo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Il colloquio non sarebbe stato dedicato soprattutto alle strategie future. Lotito e Gattuso avrebbero piuttosto fatto il punto sul lavoro delle ultime settimane, mentre i risultati sul campo accompagnano la crescita della Lazio.

Recent findings suggest that alla serenità legata al percorso della squadra si aggiunge quella nei rapporti tra società e staff tecnico. Il confronto tra presidente e allenatore riflette la volontà di procedere nella stessa direzione e di condividere gli obiettivi sportivi.

Il presidente sta mostrando maggiore interesse per la vita quotidiana del centro sportivo. Chiede aggiornamenti sulle condizioni della squadra e sull'organizzazione delle attività, seguendo più da vicino il lavoro di Gattuso.

La sua presenza vuole essere anche un segnale di sostegno allo staff tecnico e ai calciatori. Lotito intende far sentire la propria vicinanza al gruppo e accompagnare il percorso di crescita intrapreso dalla Lazio.

Tech Report: Milan-Frosinone, Amorim avverte tutti: "Sono i più veloci!". E Cardinale lo supporta

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (835 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Milannews

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that È stata una vigilia serena, quella di Milan-Frosinone a Milanello.
  • According to recent reports, una delle cose che colpisce di più del tecnico portoghese è che non si rifugia dietro frasi di circostanza ma, compatibilmente con i tempi tecnici di una conferenza, dà una spiegazione generale quando possibile.
  • Il tema caldo poteva essere quello del mercato, ma Amorim l'ha liquidato abbastanza in fretta.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that È stata una vigilia serena, quella di Milan-Frosinone a Milanello. Ma serena non vuol dire necessariamente rilassata. Ruben Amorim è tornato a parlare in conferenza stampa dopo la sosta e, come sempre, non si è sottratto dal commentare con sincerità quello che pensa della squadra di Alvini: "Il Frosinone è divertente da guardare, sono una squadra veloce, sono la squadra che sprinta di più, noi la seconda. Abbiamo le armi a disposizione per contrastare la loro velocità. Sono molto bravi nell'uno contro uno sulle fasce. È difficile capire i loro movimenti, anche se c'è qualche logica nel loro caos. Ma è difficile capire il loro stile di gioco. Ci sono superiori negli ultimi 30 metri, portano più giocatori in area, vincono molto la palla alti e non perdono tanto tempo ad avviare l'azione. Quando avremo la palla sarà importante pensare a cosa fare se dovessimo perderla. Come contro il Venezia: ci sono squadre contro cui bisogno essere molto concentrati perché possono creare grandi problemi. Mi aspetto una partita difficile, ma anche noi abbiamo un'idea calcistica che può far male agli avversari".

According to recent reports, una delle cose che colpisce di più del tecnico portoghese è che non si rifugia dietro frasi di circostanza ma, compatibilmente con i tempi tecnici di una conferenza, dà una spiegazione generale quando possibile. Ovviamente la "logica nel caos" non era una critica alla squadra ciociara, anzi. È il solito avvertimento ai calciatori, che dovranno essere veramente sul pezzo questo pomeriggio per non fare brutta figura a San Siro. Cardinale, uscendo da Milanello, ha fatto eco al suo mister: "C’è un bel clima, oggi ottimo allenamento. La squadra sta bene, ho parlato con diversi giocatori e hanno tutti sensazioni positive e capiscono mister Amorim che sottolinea quanto sia importante la partita di domani. Speriamo di vincere e di continuare in modo positivo”.

Il tema caldo poteva essere quello del mercato, ma Amorim l'ha liquidato abbastanza in fretta. Si è soffermato molto di più invece sul digiuno dal gol di Gonçalo Ramos. Solitamente gli allenatori se la sbrigano velocemente, mentre l'ex Manchester United è andato abbastanza a fondo sul problema anche qui: "Possiamo dire che magari un'opzione in più potrebbe essere una buona cosa per aiutare Camarda e Ramos, ma penso che le difficoltà di Ramos siano le difficoltà della squadra. Ho avuto due settimane per capire i dati che avete voi e che ho io. Non stiamo raggiungendo l'ultimo terzo di campo. Siamo una delle peggiori squadre nell'entrare nell'ultimo terzo e restarci. Non tiriamo molto in porta, anche se non voglio una squadra che faccia tanti tiri da fuori area perché la maggior parte delle volte non si segna da fuori area. Ma non stiamo aiutando Ramos. Cisse ha molti gol, ma in una posizione diversa. Arriva in area e quello che vedo contro il Genoa è che senza Ramos non segniamo quei due gol. Non ha segnato, ma senza Ramos non segniamo quei due gol.

Ma la mia preoccupazione più grande è la squadra ed è la quantità di volte, è il volume nella fase offensiva. Non possiamo continuare così perché stiamo segnando con questo volume molti gol, ma se pensate che possiamo mantenere questo ritmo con meno volume e più gol, non accadrà. Non saremo in grado di continuare così. Quindi il mio obiettivo è spingere la squadra in avanti. Questo è il mio lavoro, non il lavoro di Ramos, e dobbiamo spingere tutti i nostri giocatori, Ramos, Camarda, Pulisic, Rabiot, tutti questi ragazzi vicino all'area. Quindi Ramos è in difficoltà perché la squadra è in difficoltà, ma Ramos è quello che segue di più il centrocampista, il difensore centrale. So che non è il suo compito. So che abbiamo comprato un giocatore per fare gol, ma non stiamo facendo, non sto facendo il mio lavoro per aiutare Ramos, mentre Ramos sta facendo di tutto per aiutare me. E so che Ramos segnerà molti gol, ma dobbiamo spingere la squadra in avanti affinché possa giocare nella posizione di centravanti. Quindi la mia sensazione sull'ultima partita è che senza Ramos non ci sono quei gol. Ha recuperato palla, ha fatto l'assist per Pulisic. Senza Ramos non c'è gol. Quindi il mio obiettivo è vincere le partite e non importa chi segna, ma devo essere onesto con i miei giocatori. Devo fare il mio lavoro e spingere la squadra in avanti per avere più volume in attacco".

According to recent reports, anche qui il mister non si è nascosto, anzi. Intelligentemente ha tolto ogni peso, almeno mediaticamente, dalle spalle dell'ex PSG e si è preso tutte le "colpe". Dicendo tra l'altro una cosa vera: al momento il volume offensivo creato dai rossoneri non è sufficiente. C'è tanto lavoro da fare, ma a vedere i progressi fatti su vari aspetti c'è da poter essere ottimisti anche da questo punto di vista. Intanto oggi pomeriggio a San Siro ci si aspetta una gara scoppiettante, con due squadre offensive, anche se in modo differente.

Nel corso di un video sul suo canale YouTube, Alfio Musmarra, giornalista, ha parlato così delle voci di mercato riguardanti Alessandro Bastoni e il Barcellona: "L'Inter non ha necessità di vendere. Potrà vendere qualcosa nel momento in cui dovessero arrivare offerte ufficiali e formali all'altezza per un grande giocatore.

L'idea è sempre rinforzare la squadra, non depotenziarla: se poi dovesse arrivare un'offerta irrinunciabile per un substantial, verrà valutata. Se l'interesse del Barcellona nei confronti di Bastoni dovesse diventare qualcosa di più concreto ve lo diremo: ma ad oggi all'Inter non è arrivata una richiesta, una telefonata o una mail.

Può piacere al Barcellona? Sì, c'erano già stati contatti con l'entourage in estate, ma c'erano i dubbi di Flick e all'Inter non è arrivata un'offerta. Possiamo parlare di spifferi ma nulla più. Al momento è più un'idea di chi fa mercato al Barcellona che di Flick: poi se questo dovesse cambiare idea, allora il Barcellona deciderà di muoversi ufficialmente coi canali ufficiali. Ma finché non c'è nulla di concreto non ci sono indicazioni di questo tipo".

#95827. Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4850 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.
  • This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.
  • He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he noted.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

Given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

According to recent reports, that was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a newly introduced manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

Recent findings suggest that moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

Sources indicate that the victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

According to recent reports, playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

There were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

Millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

Sources indicate that millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

According to recent reports, newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

According to recent reports, so much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

Well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H.

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil noted: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

In a recent development, “We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”.

As for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”.

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

Sources indicate that the draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

Industry observers note that the third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

Still got some more post-match to come for you, but we’ve got scores from all our matches tonight now:.

Crystal Palace 3-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-3 Bradford City.

From the Champions League, Man City held out against Porto to win 2-0.

“I think we had a lot of chances in the first half, and we went in a half-time saying we need to  take our chances, so I’m glad we came out in the second half and we did,” noted Willock after the match.

Industry observers note that “100% [the competition is crucial], we’ve won it before so it’s very important to us, but every game is important to us. Especially with a new coach and a lot of new players, we wanted to start the new season well. I think we started really well and we need to continue and this was a substantial game in keeping that momentum.”.

"We stated at half-time we NEED to take our chances"Lewis Hall and Joe Willock react to Newcastle's win over Millwall 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NDF3laD8nT.

Take a look at the match-winner from Joe Willock:.

Moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The goal came minutes after Millwall were inches away from taking the lead themselves, as Arconte was denied by the post:.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

We’ll be bringing you more from the post-match now.

Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

Seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

In a recent development, willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

Newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

Industry observers note that finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

You can hear the travelling fans now!

Marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

According to recent reports, issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

Millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

According to recent reports, double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

Recent findings suggest that free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

What colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

It’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not. Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

Newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

Recent findings suggest that scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Promising restart for the home side.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:.

Crystal Palace 1-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-1 Bradford City.

Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here.

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

It has been revealed that millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

The game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

The delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

Newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

It has been revealed that gonzález is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

It has been revealed that millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

Hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

Sources indicate that newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

Industry observers note that first piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

Sources indicate that barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

In a recent development, wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

It has been revealed that another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

Again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

In a recent development, murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

According to recent reports, newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

According to recent reports, fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

Just a reminder of the teams starting today:.

Starting XI: Filip Marschall; Jordi Osei-Tutu, Caleb Taylor, Jake Cooper, Elkan Baggott; Lyndon Dykes, Jenson Metcalfe; Camiel Neghli, Daniel Kelly, Romain Esse; Zak Lovelace.

Substitutes: Regan Monty, Tristan Parkes, Sacha Vieira, George Beaumont, Yanis Issoufou, George Evans, Taïryk Arconte, Alfie Massey, Zak Sturge.

Starting XI: Lukás Hornícek; Lewis Hall, Fabian Schär, Amar Dedic, Sven Botman; Jacob Murphy, Nico González; Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Joe Willock; Yoane Wissa.

Substitutes: Tino Livramento, Anthony Elanga, Malick Thiaw, Nick Pope, Lewis Miley, Bazoumana Touré, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Aladji Bamba, Sean Steur.

It has been revealed that the teams are coming out of the tunnel, and both home and away fans in the Den are already in loud voice. Kick off on the way!

"We've tried to find the right balance" ⚖️Matthias Jaissle on his team selection for tonight's match with Millwall ⚫️ pic.twitter.com/kiRRxAgLk8.

We’re just a few minutes away from kick off in south London, but Bournemouth have scored the first goal of the third round, with Ryan Christie putting his side ahead against Lincoln.

Recent findings suggest that alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach states has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

According to recent reports, at the same time, Telegraph Sport have reported that Ross Wilson, the sporting director, has warned there will have to be more departures in future windows. Having lost Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães in 12 months, there will be yet be more upheaval.

You can read Luke Edwards’ full story on that here.

The Premier League teams playing in European competitions enter the EFL Cup in this round, with all 16 fixtures being played over five match days. As well as tonight’s games there will be:.

Peterborough United vs Barnsley (7.45pm).

Fleetwood Town vs Sheffield United (7.45pm).

Manchester City vs Norwich City (7.30pm).

*all kick-off at 8pm, unless stated otherwise.

Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

It has been revealed that jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

Bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

Aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

Having made a total of eight new signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

The visitors have arrived in south London.

We've made it to South East London 👋 pic.twitter.com/nh8Fpa37xT.

We’re bringing you the action from the pick of tonight’s EFL Cup games but there are also four games kicking off at 7.45pm:.

Crystal Palace vs Middlesbrough.

The Champions League also returns tonight and you can follow along with both our blogs:.

Aston Villa are at the moment 3-1 up against Club Brugge in Belgium – follow the action here.

Manchester City will face Porto at 8.00pm – our live blog has just gone live here with the team news from both sides.

Here is how the visitors are lining up:.

Yoane Wissa takes the captain’s armband tonight, while Jacob Ramsey starts up front after scoring a late equaliser against Bournemouth on Saturday.

Your Mags at Millwall ✊ pic.twitter.com/zfnHgTlWgh.

Here is your Millwall starting XI:.

Keeper Filip Marschall is making his debut while Jensen Metcalfe is back in the squad after his red card against Bolton was overturned on appeal.

How your Lions line-up tonight 🔢 pic.twitter.com/wEp6qLIz4Y.

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Industry observers note that newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

Alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the new season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

Lamine Yamal mercilessly taunted England rival Elliot Anderson as tensions flared during the Three Lions’ spectacular victory over Spain on Sunday night.

England held on for a memorable 3-2 victory in Madrid after Anderson was given his marching orders with just under 30 minutes remaining.

Thomas Tuchel’s side were three goals in front and cruising when Anderson - looking to atone for a sloppy error from Jarrel Quansah - cynically hauled down 19-year-old Yamal as he barrelled down on goal.

Spain were awarded a penalty for the infringement, and Anderson was sent off - much to the Manchester City star’s bemusement.

But Yamal, aggrieved by Anderson’s challenge, made a beeline for the midfielder following the challenge. According to Spanish reports, the attacker mouthed ‘tonto, tonto’ to his rival following his dismissal.

The colloquial term can mean a number of things, varying from idiot, fool or stupid, but in any case is far from a term of affection.

🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨بطاقة حمراء لإليوت أندرسون ولامين يامال يستفزه🤯🤯#اسبانيا_انجلترا #دوري_الأمم_الأوروبية pic.twitter.com/cOrswp5kCC.

Lamine Yamal was spotted taunting Elliot Anderson after the Manchester City midfielder was sent off for a challenge on the winger.

The moment came in England's historic 3-2 win over the World Champions.

Anderson blanked the 19-year-old while a VAR review confirmed the on-field official’s decision was the right one, eventually trudging off the pitch.

A fired-up Yamal galvanised the reigning world champions as they searched for an unlikely comeback.

Mikel Oyarzabal, the man who scored Spain’s winner against England two years ago in the 2024 Euros final, converted the spot kick before Nico Williams scored Spain’s second after latching on to an excellent Yamal cross.

However, Las Rojas fell short, with Sunday’s defeat their first in an imperious 43-game run.

A jubilant Thomas Tuchel hailed the match as his ‘best performance of my time as manager’.

Industry observers note that ‘What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,’ Tuchel mentioned after the game. ’Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

‘It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il Napoli Primavera non va oltre l’1 a 1 casalingo contro il Perugia. Al termine del match ha parlato il tecnico della Primavera Antonio Nocerino, ecco le sue dichiarazioni:.

According to recent reports, “Abbiamo fatto una buona gara, ma ci sono cose che a me non piacciono. Mi aspetto pochi errori e che non si sbaglia dalla gente tecnica, troppi errori nell’ultimo passaggio. La prestazione è buona, i ragazzi sono stati bravissimo, noi ieri l’abbiamo preparata che tanti erano in prima squadra. Abbiamo giocato contro una squadra che ha i punti che merita e gioca molto bene. Se andiamo a vedere la partita sono rammaricato, mi sono intristito, hai tante opportunità e non chiudi la partita, poi vabbè il rigore..sono cose che ci possono stare”.

Sulla fase difensiva: “Andando spesso uomo contro uomo, noi lavoriamo tanto sul doppio lavoro, cercando di mettersi a 1 metro e mezzo dalla distanza, sia per coprire palla nello spazio che essere pronti ad attaccare. Marotta? Al di là dell’espulsione è un giocatore molto importante per noi, dovrebbe essere più lucido nelle situazione di gara, ma questo fa parte della crescita e migliorare nella frenata e non andare di intuito, per portarlo dove vuoi tu. Ogni tanto capita l’errore, fa parte del percorso di questa stagione”.

Industry observers note that su Spinelli e Pereyra in prima squadra: “Sono contento e orgoglioso, vuol dire che il lavoro stanno facendo è giusto. Ma questo non basta, non bisogna accontentarsi, fare sempre qualche cosa in più; andare in prima squadra è bellissimo, poi bisogna farsi trovare pronto per stare più tempo e magari entrare, nel calcio non si può mai sapere”.

In a recent development, sulla Youth League: “Non siamo ancora come io vorrei, a volte devi accompagnare i ragazzi, che ancora non hanno vissuto il calcio dei grandi, piano piano stiamo cercando di fargli capire che devono essere pronti sempre. Sono bravi ragazzi e avere una mentalità forte li metterà in condizione di affrontare prime squadre. L’obiettivo è dargli autostima e meno negatività, cercando di aiutarli in questo percorso, non lasciarli abbattere. Le cose negative vengono, ma l’importante è reagire e quello è l’obiettivo che noi cerchiamo a livello emotivo”.

Industry observers note that sul Centro Sportivo: “Sicuramente deve alimentare l’entusiasmo, ormai sono tanti anni che vivo fuori e ho visto un pò tutto. A me dispiace è che si deve andare a vedere il negativo, quella cosa che non è costruttiva. Se io ho la possibilità e ho un presidente che cerca di fare qualcosa, io devo essere solo orgoglioso e onorato da napoletano, in modo che i napoletani non debbano andare via e possano avere la fortuna di essere in campi dove prepararsi fisicamente e mentalmente. Ormai quando uno fa c’è sempre qualcosa da dire, per Napoli è qualcosa che fa la differenza. Lo spero soprattutto per i ragazzi e per fargli coltivare il proprio talento. La cosa che mi sta deludendo è la negatività, non si guarda mai a chi vuole fare qualcosa di diverso che crede nella città. Chi non fa alla fine parla, deve solo parlare e buttare via l’aria alla bocca, io preferisco chi fa e alla fine sarà sempre criticato. Si tratta della mentalità italiana, c’è gelosia e invidia di chi vuole successo. A me questo dà fastidio, è un problema culturale, io nel mio piccolo sto cercando di andare avanti e non ascoltare la negatività, chi ti dirà che è facile ti sta mentendo. Mi auguro che il presidente faccia il centro sportivo, avere il centro sportivo è come l’aria”. Ecco il video:.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • When, at England's World Cup base in Kansas City, I then sat down with Trafford and he revealed that his partner had packed some Lego for him to build in camp, you wondered if sixth-form was a grade too high.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 14:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 16:35 EST, 16 November 2026.

Sources indicate that 'It was like meeting a kid at a sixth-form careers day'. That was the verdict, slightly unflattering but endearing all the same, of one Premier League chief after encountering James Trafford.

When, at England's World Cup base in Kansas City, I then sat down with Trafford and he revealed that his partner had packed some Lego for him to build in camp, you wondered if sixth-form was a grade too high.

In a recent development, he is the son of a Cumbrian farmer and the Lego was of a tractor, which he would save for later in the tournament. 'You don't want to go too early,' he noted.

Industry observers note that none of this is a criticism. Far from it. There was a boyish charm, an innocence, even, and Trafford was engaging company. Nonetheless, he did not sound ready for the likes of a World Cup semi-final against Argentina. Thomas Tuchel agreed.

But every boy will one day become a man. On a ferocious and febrile night in Madrid, no place for adolescents, we may just have witnessed James Trafford's graduation ceremony.

It has been revealed that without his double save in stoppage-time, England would have left Spain without a famous, and deserved, victory. One Spanish title labelled it 'la actuacion de su vida', the performance of his life. You wonder how much they saw of his loan spell at Accrington Stanley, but the sentiment stands.

James Trafford celebrates with Jarell Quansah, Dan Burn and Ezri Konsa during his starring performance in Spain.

Trafford pictured with his farmer father, David, in the cab of his tractor with their dogs (Source: James Trafford).

Madrid daily AS exclaimed: 'Magisterio de Trafford!' Translated, 'A Trafford Masterclass!'. They claim he was the reason Spain could not complete their comeback, and they would be right.

When Tuchel stood with us in a corridor of the Metropolitano Stadium on the eve of the game, he had no issue confirming that Trafford would start. His message, though, was clear - it was sink or swim for a goalkeeper who turned 24 last month.

Recent findings suggest that not only did Trafford keep his head above water, it was he who pulled the team ashore. It was he to whom his senior colleagues ran in celebration. Ezri Konsa nearly took the shirt off Trafford's back, such was the force of his gratitude. But maybe this was the occasion when Trafford took the No 1 jersey from the back of Jordan Pickford, the holder for nearly a decade.

It has been revealed that pickford has done nothing wrong. Were Trafford to still display that maturity deficit, Pickford would be a reliable custodian heading to Euro 2028. This is not Peter Shilton post Italia 90, an uncomfortable truth of a great in need of the retirement barn. The 32-year-old has plenty to give on the back of all he has already given.

This, admitted Tuchel after the 3-2 win, is a selection dilemma that allows a manager to sleep well at night.

'There is no headache at all!' he boomed. 'I'm so far away from a headache, I cannot imagine.

Trafford left Manchester City with the strategy to usurp Jordan Pickford as England No 1.

Jude Bellingham certainly seemed impressed with the performance of the goalkeeper.

'This is what we wanted. This is the best thing that can happen to all of us, also to Pickers. It is amazing how they push each other, and if then Traff has a performance like this, he has it because he knows he's well prepared. He gets the push from his colleagues and competitors.'.

Sources indicate that tuchel has seen enough of Trafford in training and around camp to believe he is ready for promotion. He has watched him for Leeds, where he rates as the best performing goalkeeper in the Premier League. His 'net goals prevented' (4.4) and 'save percentage' (81.4) are higher than any rival this season, including Pickford.

In a recent development, 'You always have to deserve your place,' added Tuchel. 'You will never get a gift and just get a game (for the sake of it). So he deserved to play and we expected this kind of performance. It was not only the last save, but also the build-up play and not losing focus. He has proved it on this stage, so this gives him a lot of belief. Now, it's on him to keep going for it.'.

In a recent development, it, you presume, is the No 1 jersey. Trafford has made no secret of his desire to take it from Pickford, and he told us in the summer that such ambition was the motivation behind him wanting to leave Manchester City for a second time.

That day, he flipped his room key with a magician's sleight of hand throughout the interview, a dexterity useful for Lego. Better still for fingertip saves such as the one to deny Aymeric Laporte in the 91st minute.

Also in the gift pack from his girlfriend were two face masks. 'Very thoughtful,' he quipped. But that is another observation, bordering on concern, that some prospective buyers have made in recent years - on the goalkeeping scale of uber professional to joker, he resides too close to the latter. We have seen, even this season, the odd concentration lapse that speaks to that thought.

Trafford has played a starring role in goal since moving to Leeds United in the summer.

Sources indicate that but there was also a feeling that Trafford needed more exposure and responsibility before the penny dropped and his value was realised. Already, £95million has been spent on him in transfer fees.

According to recent reports, at Leeds, and now with England, he has been given that stage, as Tuchel calls it. The head coach maintains that Pickford is his first choice, but it was Trafford he picked for both Nations League fixtures against Spain, the ones that really mattered, the ones that would strengthen or threaten his own employment.

As for Trafford's career prospects, to revisit our opening line, England's No 1 sounds like a fair vocation.

Thomas Tuchel wants England to use victory in the Nations League finals as a springboard to winning Euro 2028 at Wembley.

The head coach admits it has taken him a while to recover from the trauma of his side’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July, for which he was heavily criticised.

But after beating world champions Spain 3-2 on Sunday night, topping their Nations League group ahead of March’s quarter-finals and next summer's finals, Tuchel is finally able to look forward with positivity and belief.

Industry observers note that ‘I saw the celebrations in Portugal when they won the Nations League,’ he stated. ‘It’s just the best, the best preparation we can have for the Euros. We want to have these matches on the highest level to prove ourselves and to gain confidence, to see where we are and to adjust our game where we need to, that’s what this Nations League is perfect for. We want to win it.’.

England have won five of their six matches since the World Cup, losing only to Spain at Wembley in September. In the build up to that game, Tuchel was involved in heated exchanges with observers who continued to question his tactics in the final half hour against Argentina.

’It took me a while to digest (the World Cup exit) and see the way forward, how we can help and adjust and improve, and how we can do this together,’ he said.

Sources indicate that ‘We had reviews and so on, but clarity then came together with the players. Straight away we had the energy right to take the next steps. The ideas became more clear for me, even if it was not so easy the first week, to overcome and arrive with different emotions. Some were still upset from the World Cup. Some were new in the team. Some had digested it, some had not digested it. But it was key to have this kind of process together.

Industry observers note that ‘(Spain) was a complete performance that makes me very proud. It's a full package of belief, of courage, of commitment, of togetherness, of relying on each other and stepping up in this moment.’.

Tuchel, though, has rejected the idea that seeing out the win Madrid was proof that he has learned from his mistakes in Atlanta.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Not at all, I think we would not have been in this situation if it was 11 against 11,’ he noted. ‘For me, it was Mexico reloaded (not Argentina). It's one man down, but what can you do? It is their strength to have ball possession, to overload and find the gaps. It just plays totally into their hands and it comes wave after wave. It felt like three hours and thirty minutes!’.

Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5250 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.
  • So much for the latest group stage of the competition taking time to warm up.
  • And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

So much for the latest group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

It has been revealed that city will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

It has been revealed that there is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

Recent findings suggest that they wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

Sources indicate that “I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a new team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

It has been revealed that phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

Bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

Recent findings suggest that “In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This highlights how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

By Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Recent findings suggest that diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

It has been revealed that city had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Sources indicate that enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

Recent findings suggest that “It is a hard place to come [Porto],” stated Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

Recent findings suggest that porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

Sources indicate that “We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli noted. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Questo pomeriggio, ore 18.00, il Milan accoglie il Frosinone di Alvini a San Siro. Una gara insidiosa per diversi motivi: è la prima dopo la sosta, le altre squadre lì in alto - Lazio, Roma e Como - hanno vinto e i ciociari hanno uno stile di gioco offensivo e difficile da gestire. Fabio Capello, intervistato dalla Gazzetta dello Sport, nel commentare queste prime battute del dodicesimo turno di Serie A si sofferma anche sui rossoneri. Queste le sue parole:.

Il Milan, dal canto suo, deve restare aggrappato al treno delle prime.

"Con il Frosinone è una partita fondamentale, perché la squadra di Alvini sa ripartire a velocità folle, mentre i rossoneri soffrono quando perdono palla. Io, però, mi aspetto che il Milan faccia il Milan e questa è la gara giusta per dimostrare di essere all’altezza".

La Primavera del Napoli pareggia 1-1 contro il Perugia, è il terzo pareggio consecutivo in campionato dopo quelli contro Monopoli e Frosinone. La zona play-off è distante sempre cinque punti, il Bari quinto in classifica ha pareggiato contro il Catanzaro. #95809. Thomas Tuchel is now embracing traditional English values - clarity has helped England understand who they are, and now they can beat the best, writes CRAIG HOPE

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (943 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Thomas Tuchel is now embracing traditional English values - clarity has helped England understand who they are, and now they can beat the best, writes CRAIG HOPE

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (943 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Thomas Tuchel has always liked what he sees from his England players on the training pitch.
  • It is why, when the squad reconvened at St George’s Park in September, Tuchel used the meeting room as much as he did the grass to address that disparity in delivery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026.

Thomas Tuchel has always liked what he sees from his England players on the training pitch. Less so, at times, inside a stadium. It is a contradiction with which he has wrestled since the World Cup, when performances on the whole left him underwhelmed, save for the collective spirit and individual excellence that rescued results.

It is why, when the squad reconvened at St George’s Park in September, Tuchel used the meeting room as much as he did the grass to address that disparity in delivery.

Sources indicate that at the same time, the elephant in the corner of the auditorium was the German’s own comments about the DNA of English players compared to the likes of Spain, and fundamentally them lacking the coding to protect possession and, therefore, valuable leads. He asked Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and others for their thoughts.

In a recent development, the message back from his players was this – let us be better at being us, not them. Interestingly, that was Tuchel’s mantra upon his appointment, one of embracing traditional English values. Amid the World Cup fallout, though, he had wandered in a daze down a rabbit hole of genetics, focusing on what his team cannot do as opposed to what they can.

Industry observers note that tuchel, his staff and his players are tacticians and technicians, not scientists. If the intricacies of DNA do not allow them to be Spain, then don’t be. Be England, they determined. That is not to say kick and rush, bark and bite. After all, Kane is officially the best player in the world right now and Bellingham, unofficially, is playing as well as anyone on the planet.

Recent findings suggest that rather, there needed to be clarity – this is what we are and this is how we beat the best. On Sunday night in Madrid, England beat the very best. It was a victory born from those hours on the training field and in conference, and even more spent by Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry during their post-tournament review in a St George’s Park war room. They knew then that this was not a case of rip it up and start again, more so mend the tears and give the likes of Bellingham a blank sheet to impact where, and how, he sees best.

Thomas Tuchel is embracing England's DNA and reaping the rewards following the World Cup.

England can now beat the best, which they showed against Spain in a fantastic victory.

Industry observers note that there was no radical strategical change, but there was a newly introduced doctrine, principles that should underpin whatever the in-game circumstance – off-the-ball running, a high press, filling in for a team-mate who has seized a moment to improvise elsewhere, such as the full backs. Ben White scoring England’s third on Sunday and Lewis Hall completing four more dribbles than Lamine Yamal were examples of Tuchel’s allowance for greater intuition. Be you, not Spain.

Kane, informally at least, has also been promoted beyond captain, a bridge between management and dressing-room. To see him in a semi-coaching and cajoling capacity on the touchline after he was taken off in the 78th minute against Spain was to witness this elevation.

According to recent reports, but even if England had conceded a late equaliser at the Metropolitano Stadium, it would not have mattered. Not when it comes to measuring post World Cup improvement. To have drawn comparison with Argentina and that second-half collapse would have been unfair and inaccurate. The semi-final was 11 versus 11 and so let us judge this game on the same terms. And what did England do with a 1-0 lead and 11 players? They attacked. And attacked again. For all of the tweaks Tuchel and Barry have made to the structure of training and the team’s set-up, this was evidence of them learning from a mistake, as much as the head coach will be loath to admit.

Ezri Konsa, however, did reveal there was a definite instruction to keep attacking Spain when Tuchel addressed the team at half-time.

Industry observers note that ‘The instruction was to keep going at them,’ noted the defender. ‘Don’t stop. To keep our foot on the pedal. That is what we did. Argentina was different, different circumstances. But it was not just half-time. We went 1-0 up and Harry, our captain, told us to keep going and to keep our foot on the pedal too.'.

In a recent development, before Jarell Quansah’s needless mistake and Elliot Anderson’s subsequent dismissal in the 63rd minute, the game was not in the balance in any way. As a live observer of almost every Tuchel match since his arrival, this was the best performance of his reign. In fact, it’s not even close.

And yet, so much still comes back to Bellingham. England would not have won without him. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his powers. Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too. His swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. He won the corner for Konsa’s headed second and created the third for White. He then dropped into midfield when down to ten and battled and organised like a captain.

In a recent development, bellingham has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his big ideas. For now, they don’t come much bigger than what England achieved in Madrid.

Mattia Marello, esterno sinistro dell'Inter U23 e autore del primo gol nella vittoria contro il Potenza, ha parlato in conferenza stampa al termine del match: "Sono super contento per la squadra e per il mio gol perché ha contribuito alla vittoria. In a recent development, cosa scatta nella testa di ragazzi come te alla prima esperienza tra i professionisti quando si è chiamati ad affrontare squadre di categoria? Cosa vi viene chiesto?

"Venivamo da una settimana difficile, io come tanti altri siamo stati in Nazionale, altri erano con la Prima Squadra, e quindi non siamo riusciti ad allenarci bene. Abbiamo preparato la partita in pochi giorni, ma sono stati molto importanti perché abbiamo fatto gruppo. Il mister ci ha parlato tanto prima e dopo l'allenamento, ci ha detto molto del Potenza insieme al suo staff e l'abbiamo preparata alla grande. Eravamo gasati".

Difficile preparare una gara con l'uscita di GTA?

Recent findings suggest that "GTA? Non ho la Play Station, non è un mio problema... Magari altri hanno sofferto questo momento, ma non è il mio caso! Sono molto contento per la partita, eravamo gasati anche prima, il mister ci ha fatto un bel discorso e ci ha preparati. Sapevamo che non sarebbe stata una partita come le altre".

In cosa puoi migliorare ancora?

"Parlo sempre tanto con il mister e i suoi collaboratori, lo chiedo anche io. Io cerco di migliorarmi ogni giorno su tutto, anche sulle cose in cui sono più forte, però principalmente cerco di allenare il piede debole e le letture difensive per diventare un calciatore completo".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that cosa c'entra un videogame con il calcio?
  • Recent findings suggest that il lancio è stato ovviamente globale e questa curiosità è arrivata nelle sale stampa anche dei club di Serie A.
  • Gattuso: "Io non so nemmeno cos'è GTA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that cosa c'entra un videogame con il calcio? C'entra eccome. Intanto quello di GTA VI è un fenomeno mediatico assoluto e difficilmente ripetibile: in 24 ore ha fatto registrare 32.5 milioni di copie vendute, per un incasso di 3.79 miliardi di dollari (!), per quello che è il più grande lancio della storia di un prodotto di intrattenimento. Nei mesi scorsi Steven Adams, che gioca a basket in NBA, aveva detto tra il serio ed il faceto che l'uscita del gioco avrebbe avuto un impatto anche sul mondo dello sport professionistico: "Vi dirò una cosa: preparatevi per novembre. Le prestazioni del campionato caleranno, a livello generale, perché uscirà GTA. Guardate la NFL, guardate tutti i campionati e vedrete come precipiteranno. Solo per il mese di novembre, ma le prestazioni caleranno. Dovrebbero però risalire. La maggior parte dei ragazzi ce la farà, speriamo che portino a termine il gioco. Lo stesso vale per gli allenatori, tra l’altro. Gli staff tecnici saranno terribili, solo per novembre, ma dovrebbero riprendersi a dicembre. Speriamo".

Recent findings suggest that il lancio è stato ovviamente globale e questa curiosità è arrivata nelle sale stampa anche dei club di Serie A. È stata fatta la stessa domanda - ovvero se fossero preoccupati dal fatto che i calciatori potessero fare le ore piccole - a Gennaro Gattuso, Ruben Amorim e Cesc Fabregas, che hanno risposto così:.

Gattuso: "Io non so nemmeno cos'è GTA. Un videogioco? Lo scopro ora, mi sembrava una macchina con quel nome. Se i miei ci giocheranno di notte saranno cazzi loro, non mi metto a controllare e a chiedere a un calciatore se ha giocato con la PlayStation. Per il lavoro che si fa ci vuole amor proprio, durante la colazione insieme proverò a capire se qualcuno ha fatto le ore piccole". A vedere da come ha giocato la Lazio contro il Lecce probabilmente nessuno è rimasto alzato tutta la notte.

Recent findings suggest that amorim invece ha usato toni più scherzosi: "Faccio rispondere il mio amico Gattuso (ride, ndr). Non mi interessa. Devono essere pronti, se non sono pronti un altro prende il suo posto. Modric penso che non conosca neanche questo gioco. Gattuso ha già detto tutto (ride, ndr)".

Fabregas invece è stato un po' più sostenuto, rivelando un malcontento per le tematiche affrontate nel videogioco: "Non farmi parlare di questo (ride, ndr). Speriamo che non ci giochi nessuno a questo gioco. Specialmente i nostri figli”. Tranquillo Cesc, il PEGI 18 serve proprio ad indicare che si tratta di un prodotto con tematiche mature. Proprio come succede con i film.

Breaking: Scotland skipper Andy Robertson insists time is running out for Pocognoli's men after horror show in St Gallen
